channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran Reportedly Escalating Efforts to Assassinate US Officials Abroad
item.description: An intelligence memo obtained by Axios indicates Iran has significantly increased efforts to target US officials outside the United States, with some plots reaching advanced stages. US officials cited these concerns as a reason for reducing embassy staffing in the Middle East.

item.title: Tashkent Air Quality Reaches "Very Unhealthy" Levels in Some Areas
item.description: Tashkent's air quality has reached "very unhealthy" levels in certain areas. The deterioration occurred overnight between October 23rd and 24th, attributed to falling temperatures, weak winds, and temperature inversions.

item.title: Five Children Rescued from Apartment Fire in Karaganda
item.description: Eight people, including five children, were rescued by emergency services from a fire in a residential building in Karaganda. Another seven residents were evacuated. No injuries were reported. The fire involved furniture and belongings on the fourth floor of a nine-story building.

item.title: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang Visits Kazakhstan, Discusses AI Nation Strategy
item.description: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang made his first visit to Kazakhstan, meeting with the Minister of Digital Development. Huang stated that Kazakhstan is the first country he has visited where the president has declared an intention to transform the nation into an AI nation. He believes AI will elevate Kazakhstan's economy and create new opportunities for citizens and companies.

item.title: Three-Year-Old Girl Falls into Coma After Dental Treatment in Pavlodar
item.description: A three-year-old girl in Pavlodar has fallen into a coma following dental treatment, confirmed by the regional health department. Relatives reported the child experienced breathing difficulties during the procedure. The clinic stated they follow all medical protocols, while the girl remains in intensive care.

item.title: Kazakhstan Establishes Medal in Honor of Gaziz Baitasov
item.description: Kazakhstan has established a departmental medal of the Ministry of Internal Affairs named after Gaziz Baitasov. The award, initiated by the President, will recognize law enforcement officers for courage and heroism in the line of duty. The first medal was presented to Baitasov's wife. Gaziz Baitasov, a police captain, died in 2011 while apprehending a terrorist.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Health Ministry Opposes 'Tips' for Medical Workers
item.description: The Ministry of Health of Kyrgyzstan has spoken out against the practice of monetary gratitude for medical workers, even if patients wish to pay through official channels. An official stated that doctors' salaries have been increased since April 2026, making them sufficient. The ministry believes that even voluntary monetary tips could negatively impact the healthcare system over time.

item.title: Akmzhan Festival Gathers Top Agrarians of Kyzylorda Region
item.description: The 'Akmzhan' agro-cultural festival in the Kyzylorda region concluded with the 'Golden Autumn - 2026' ceremony, honoring the best agricultural workers. The region allocated 37 billion tenge for agricultural support this year, a 1.5-fold increase from the previous year. Production in the sector reached 178 billion tenge in nine months.

item.title: State Awards Presented in Atyrau on Kazakhstan's Republic Day
item.description: On the eve of Republic Day, the Akim of Atyrau region, Bolat Akchulakov, presented state awards on behalf of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to citizens who contributed to the country's development. The awards recognized individuals from various sectors including industry, energy, agriculture, education, and culture.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Second Month of Declining Food Prices, Government Reports
item.description: Food prices in Kazakhstan have decreased for the second consecutive month, according to the government. While the monthly decline is 0.1%, year-to-date prices for socially significant goods have risen by 1.8%. Some vegetables have seen price increases due to colder weather, prompting plans for producer agreements and more agricultural fairs.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker Meets Compatriots During Official Visit to Japan
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Kyrgyz Parliament, met with Kyrgyz citizens living and working in Japan during an official visit. Discussions focused on strengthening ties with expatriates, protecting their rights, and developing cultural and economic cooperation between Kyrgyzstan and Japan.

item.title: UN Special Representative Vows Continued Support for Afghan People
item.description: Rabab Fatima, the UN Special Representative for Afghanistan, has pledged continued support for the Afghan people. Marking the UN's 81st anniversary, she expressed deep respect for Afghanistan's culture and heritage, committing to listen to and work with its people as they shape their future.

item.title: Tajikistan to database sorcerers, clients, and drug addicts
item.description: Tajikistan's Interior Ministry has created a special database to record information on fortune tellers, sorcerers, prostitutes, their clients, relatives, and drug addicts. The aim is to prevent the spread of superstition and similar practices. Individuals listed will be under constant surveillance.

item.title: UN Chief Links Global Protests to Economic Fallout of Conflicts
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned violence during protests worldwide, linking public discontent to expanding armed conflicts and their economic consequences. He noted rising prices for essentials and interest rates, making future prospects difficult for youth. Guterres stressed that while violence is unacceptable, the root causes of peaceful protests must be addressed.

item.title: Moscow Deploys Armed Military Personnel and Anti-Aircraft Machine Guns on Lenin Mausoleum Roof
item.description: Following mass drone attacks from Ukraine, Moscow has intensified security measures, deploying armed military personnel on the roof of the Lenin Mausoleum and surrounding the area with armored vehicles equipped with anti-aircraft machine guns. This action is part of heightened security protocols in response to perceived threats.

item.title: Almaty Conference Discusses Accelerating Progress on UN Sustainable Development Goals
item.description: A conference in Almaty highlighted that only about 16% of Sustainable Development Goals show sufficient progress for achievement by 2030, with areas like hunger eradication and clean water stagnating. Kazakhstan ranks 67th globally in SDG achievement, showing good progress in poverty reduction but moderate progress in health and economic growth.

item.title: Kazakhstan sees second consecutive month of falling inflation
item.description: Kazakhstan's inflation has decreased for the second consecutive month, with food prices showing a deflationary trend of -0.1%. The Ministry of Trade and Integration reported that prices for sugar, onions, apples, carrots, and rice have fallen. Measures are being taken to stabilize prices, including agricultural fairs and special promotions.

item.title: Kazakhstan may deny accreditation to foreign media citing national security interests
item.description: A new order by Tleuberdi allows for foreign media to be denied accreditation based on national security interests. This move could impact the operations of international news organizations within Kazakhstan, potentially restricting access and reporting capabilities. The specific criteria for denial remain subject to interpretation.

item.title: Tajikistan's Health Sector Funding Triples in Five Years, Minister Reports
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Health and Social Protection, Jamoliddin Abdullozoda, announced that healthcare funding has increased 2.5 times over the past five years. He made these remarks at the Global Summit on Child Wellbeing in Samarkand, emphasizing child health as a state policy priority. Investments in youth health strengthen human capital and promote sustainable development.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Extending Travel Ban for Tax Debtors to Four Months
item.description: In Kazakhstan, 705 taxpayers owe a total of 931 billion tenge in taxes. The State Revenue Committee reported that individuals with debts exceeding 27,000 MCI (116.8 million tenge) may face temporary travel bans. Currently, a three-month period of non-payment can trigger this restriction, but a proposal is being considered to extend it to four months.

item.title: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Ballistic Missile Over Riyadh
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition announced it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Riyadh. Saudi air defenses successfully neutralized the threat early Saturday morning. Emergency alerts were issued in several regions, including Riyadh and Najran, following the incident. The coalition also reported intercepting a drone in eastern Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Afghan Activist Calls for Continued Aid and Support for Women's Rights
item.description: Mina Sharif, an Afghan author and activist, discussed the control of narratives and representation of Afghan people under Taliban rule. She emphasized the ongoing need for international aid and support for the rights of Afghan women and girls. The discussion took place within the context of 8AM Media's podcast series focusing on Afghanistan's situation since August 2021.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Tighten Social Assistance Criteria from 2027
item.description: Starting January 2027, Kazakhstan will introduce stricter conditions for receiving social benefits and targeted social assistance. Key requirements include full disclosure of banking and credit history for all family members. Aid will be denied if families possess savings exceeding 200 MCI, more than one dwelling unit, or commercial property. Benefits will be automatically frozen for families deemed financially secure.

item.title: China Advocates Against Space Becoming New Military Conflict Zone
item.description: China has presented its position on global space governance, outlining ten core principles. The nation proposes strengthening international space regulations, preventing an arms race, and enhancing information exchange on launches, satellite collisions, and space debris. Beijing emphasizes maintaining space for peaceful purposes and supports a legally binding international instrument for arms control in space.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Build 100-Bed Hospital in Kerben Next Year
item.description: A 100-bed General Practice Center is planned for construction in Kerben next year, President Sadyr Japarov announced during a working trip to Jalal-Abad region. He also highlighted the district's budget growth and the commissioning of two small hydropower plants. Priorities include providing clean drinking water, developing irrigation, and reclaiming arid lands.

item.title: Deputy head of Kosonsoy district arrested for accepting bribe
item.description: The deputy head of Kosonsoy district in Namangan region was arrested on suspicion of accepting a bribe. He allegedly threatened an entrepreneur to transfer land rights if solar panels were not installed. He was apprehended while receiving 65 million soums.

item.title: First medal named after Gaziz Baitasov awarded to his wife
item.description: The first medal named after Gaziz Baitasov has been awarded to his wife, Gulzhamal Tazhiyeva. This medal, established by presidential decree, honors internal affairs officers who show bravery in the line of duty. Baitasov died protecting civilians during a 2011 terrorist operation.

item.title: Head of Social Protection Department Found Dead in Atyrau Apartment
item.description: The head of the Social Protection Department for the Atyrau region, Rauirzhan Asainov, was found dead in his apartment on October 18. Sources suggest his body may have been undiscovered for about two weeks. Preliminary information points to a possible conflict with his brother after consuming alcohol, though official confirmation is pending. Asainov had led the department since January 2023.

item.title: Uzbekistan Eases Fines for Exporters Facing Payment Delays
item.description: Uzbekistan's Legislative Chamber approved amendments to reduce fines by half for exporters unable to repatriate foreign trade assets on time. The changes aim to protect businesses facing delays due to foreign counterparty actions or international payment system restrictions. In 2024, economic courts fined 3,500 entrepreneurs 752 billion soums.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Oman Launch Direct Air Service with Astana-Salalah Route
item.description: Kazakhstan and Oman have inaugurated direct air service with the launch of the Astana-Salalah route by Air Astana. The first flight carried 140 passengers. This initiative aligns with Kazakhstan's goal to expand international flights and strengthen its position as an aviation hub. A prior agreement on air transport was signed between the two governments.

item.title: UN Office Emphasizes Continued Humanitarian Assistance for Afghan Families
item.description: The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) stressed the critical need for Afghan families to access food and healthcare services. OCHA is supporting families across Afghanistan with humanitarian partners to help them cope with crises and improve living conditions, highlighting the impact of economic and climate crises on millions.

item.title: Zelensky: Starlink Restrictions Remain Despite Trump's Comments
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that restrictions on the speed of Starlink satellite communication systems and their military counterpart, Starshield, remain in effect across Ukraine. He noted that the delivery of anti-ballistic missile interceptors, crucial for defense against Russian attacks, is also delayed, complicating battlefield operations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Decreased Prices for Certain Food Products
item.description: Kazakhstan's food inflation has slowed for the second consecutive month, with a deflationary trend of 0.1%. Prices for sugar, onions, apples, carrots, and lamb decreased last week, while bread, pasta, butter, salt, and tea prices remained stable.

item.title: New Comfort-Class Building in Shchuchinsk Lacks Adequate Heating, Residents Complain
item.description: Residents of a newly constructed comfort-class apartment building in Shchuchinsk, Akmola region, are struggling with insufficient heating despite the official start of the heating season. Radiators remain cold, forcing residents to use electric heaters to maintain a minimum temperature of 18 degrees Celsius, incurring additional costs.

item.title: UN Envoy: Afghan Talents and Aspirations Greater Than Challenges
item.description: The head of UNAMA stated that the talents, aspirations, and potential of the Afghan people are greater than the challenges they face. He reaffirmed the UN's commitment to supporting Afghans and praised their resilience.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP Addresses Land Grabbing Allegations in Bazar-Korgon
item.description: Member of Parliament Aybek Altynbekov has responded to accusations of illegally using land and seizing a market in the Bazar-Korgon district. He stated that disputes should be resolved based on documents and law, not personal opinions. President Sadyr Japarov has ordered an investigation into the land use.

item.title: Trump Considered 200% Tariffs on Ukraine and Russia to End Conflict
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump stated he considered imposing 200% tariffs on Ukraine and Russia if they did not reach a peace agreement. He claimed this tactic helped end five wars but expressed doubt about its effectiveness in this specific case due to limited US trade with both nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Ukraine Sign Memorandum on Cooperation in Pharmaceutical Regulation
item.description: Uzbekistan and Ukraine have signed a memorandum of cooperation in pharmaceutical regulation. A Ukrainian delegation visited Tashkent to discuss experiences in developing healthcare systems, drug reimbursement mechanisms, and ensuring affordable medicines. The agreement aims to facilitate Ukrainian drug exports to Uzbekistan.

item.title: Central Asia's Heritage Presented at the UN in Geneva
item.description: Uzbekistan's Center for Islamic Civilization showcased the region's scientific and spiritual heritage at an international exhibition and conference in Geneva. The event brought together diplomats, international organization representatives, scholars, and cultural figures to discuss new scientific and educational projects. It highlighted the contributions of scholars from Bukhara, Samarkand, and Termez to world civilization.

item.title: Akyin Askat Zhetigen Announces Entry into Politics
item.description: Renowned akyin Askat Zhetigen has declared his intention to enter politics, stating his commitment to realizing his political views constructively. He plans to continue his cultural work, promoting Kyrgyz history, traditional music, and art internationally. Zhetigen previously faced charges related to public calls for riots and power seizure.
